m: Salutation to Shri Ganesha. The seer said: The blessed one named Nanda, who will be born of Nanda, when praised, worshipped, and meditated upon, would bring the three worlds under her will.
Her lustre is of the finest gold. She wears a beautiful garment of gold. The Goddess shines with the colour of gold and is adorned with the finest gold.
Her four arms are adorned with a golden goad, a noose, and lotuses. She is Idira, Kamala, Lakshmi, Shri, seated on a golden lotus.
The Goddess whom I have named Raktadantika, O faultless one — I will describe her form. Listen. It takes away all fear.
She wears a red garment, is red in colour, and is adorned with red on every limb. Her weapons are red, her eyes are red, her hair is red, and she is exceedingly terrible.
Her sharp nails are red, her teeth are red, and her fangs are red. As a woman is devoted to her husband, the Goddess attends the devotee.
She is as broad as the earth itself. Her two breasts are like twin Sumerus, long, pendulous, very full, and exceedingly beautiful.
They are firm and very lovely, oceans of the milk of all joy. The Goddess would give her devotees to drink from those two breasts, which yield every wish.
She bears a sword, a vessel, a pestle, and a plough. She is called the red Chamunda, and also the Goddess Yogeshvari.
By her the whole world, what stands still and what moves, is pervaded. The devotee who worships her pervades what moves and what does not move.
The Goddess attends the person who recites this praise of Raktadanti's body every day, as a woman attends a dear husband.
Shakambhari is dark blue in colour, her eyes like blue lotuses, her navel deep, and her slender body adorned with the three folds.
Her breasts are firm, very high, round, full, and dense. Dwelling in the lotus, she holds a fist full of arrows and a lotus.
She holds a mass of vegetables rich in flowers, sprouts, roots, and fruits, joined with the juices of desired foods, taking away hunger, thirst, death, and old age.
The supreme sovereign also bears a bow of flashing beauty. Shakambhari is Shatakshi, and she herself is famed as Durga.
Praising Shakambhari, meditating, reciting, fully worshipping, and bowing, one quickly obtains food, drink, and the rest, unfailing and complete.
Bhima too is dark blue, shining with fangs and teeth, a woman with wide eyes and breasts that are round, full, and dense.
Bearing the moon-smile sword, a damaru drum, and a skull-cup, she is called Ekavira and Kalaratri, and when praised she grants what is desired.
Hard to assail within her circle of splendour, bearing a wonderful beauty, resembling a many-coloured bee, she is sung of as Mahamari, Bhramari.
These, lord of the earth, are the forms of the Goddess that have been set forth. They are declared to be the wish-yielding cows of Chandika, Mother of the world.
This supreme secret should not be told to just anyone. Recite for yourself, with attention, this account of the divine forms.

The meditation on the Goddess has been told to you, great, more secret than the secret, giving, with every effort, the fruit of every desire. Thus the secret of the forms in the Devi Mahatmya, in the Savarnika manvantara of the Markandeya Purana, is complete.
